newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul subway to start operating at end-1998.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul subway to start operating at end-1998.

text.p: Istanbul mayor Recep Tayyip Erdogan said on Tuesday the first phase of the construction of Istanbul's subway link between Taksim-4.Levent districts would be fully completed at end-1998.

"As Istanbul Municipality, we have finished 80 percent of the digging for the subway project and planning to complete the first link from Taksim to 4.Levent at end-1998," Erdogan told a "Public Private Investment in Infrastructure" seminar organised by the World Bank in Istanbul.
The $262 million Taksim-4.Levent subway construction had begun in 1992, with the electro-mechanical system tender awarded to a consortium led by Turk Siemens, largely owned by German Siemens AG.
Erdogan said a project to build a tube tunnel under Istanbul's Bosphorus strait to link its Asian and European parts was also planned to ease the city's heavy traffic load.
He did not give further details about the project which will supplement Istanbul's two bridges over the Bosphorus which are usually jammed.

"To ease the traffic tension in Istanbul, we prepared projects for a 13 km-long, light railway project for the European side and a 30 km-long one for the Asian side," Erdogan said, adding that $75 million was spent to increase ferry transport between the two sides.
